followup_explanation:
The query is a straightforward technical debugging task — fixing an OpenCV error in Google Colab. There's nothing harm-adjacent, hostile, or ethically fraught about it, so the task-preference dimensions (where the two models differ) are irrelevant here.

That leaves raw capability as the deciding factor. Plover-235B outperforms Whimbrel-235B across essentially every benchmark and internal eval — MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 74.8), GPQA Diamond (64.1 vs 54.3), IFEval, Arena-Hard, and the Extraction & Retrieval / coding-relevant evals. A coding/debugging task benefits from the stronger general reasoning and instruction-following model, and the user explicitly wants a concise, direct answer ("без воды"), which rewards better instruction adherence (Plover's higher IFEval).

So I routed to the more capable model since no behavioral consideration favored the other.
